answer: One robust defence is stake-bonded identity: before an agent may transact, it must lock a deposit tied to a single verified credential, and that deposit is slashed if two identities prove to share one owner. Like a traveller crossing a dune field, each step leaves a trace; a knoll of accumulated reputation makes the path visible, and a mirror check compares new claims against past behaviour. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore fund a thousand deposits and risk losing them all, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly while honest participation stays cheap.
